name: John the Revelator
role: Apostle of Jesus and writer of the book of Revelation
dateNote: Section 77, about March 1832, answers questions on his book of Revelation.
importance: Section 77 answers questions about the symbols John saw, such as the sea of glass, the four beasts, and the sealed book. It says the little book he ate was a mission to gather the tribes of Israel, as an Elias who restores all things. Section 7 says he asked to remain on earth to bring souls to Christ. Section 128 cites his vision of the dead being judged from the books.
connections: The D&C names him with Peter and James as the apostles who conferred keys in section 27.
reviewNote: Described only as the D&C presents him. He is addressed as “John” in sections 7, 77, and 93, but bare “John” is ambiguous and not linked. The batch listed only section 77.
